questions.promptMd: In scaled dot-product attention the raw scores are divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$ before the softmax. Why?

options.textMd: To make the weights sum to 1
To keep scores from growing with vector dimension so the softmax does not saturate

questions.explanationMd: Dot products of random vectors grow like $\sqrt{d_k}$. Without the scaling, large scores push the softmax into a near one-hot regime where gradients vanish. Summing to 1 is the softmax's job, not the scaling's.

questions.promptMd: Which single operation guarantees that each row of attention weights sums to 1?
questions.explanationMd: Softmax exponentiates the scores and divides by their sum, so every row is a probability distribution over the keys.

questions.promptMd: What is the cosine similarity of a non-zero vector with itself?
questions.explanationMd: Cosine similarity is the dot product divided by the product of the norms, which is exactly 1 when the two vectors are identical -- the angle between them is zero.
